idiom_name: Exposed forUpdate() on a query, or the JPA LockModeType.PESSIMISTIC_WRITE path on Kotlin
implementation_notes: Exposed marks a select as a locking read with forUpdate() (AbstractQuery exposes isForUpdate and hasCustomForUpdateState), executed inside a transaction {} block; on a JPA/Hibernate stack the Java path applies unchanged (LockModeType.PESSIMISTIC_WRITE, Spring Data @Lock). In both cases the row lock ends with the transaction, so the offline lease is the lock record with owner and timeout, and the classic structure remains the only way to keep the claim across the requests of one business transaction.
pitfalls: Exposed transactions are thread-bound: suspending inside transaction {} and resuming on another thread (instead of newSuspendedTransaction) loses the transaction context and with it the lock.

forUpdate() is dialect-gated - dialects that cannot express row locks emit nothing, and the generated SQL has regressed before (Exposed changelog, EXPOSED-827), so assert the SQL for the target database.
On the JPA path PESSIMISTIC_WRITE rolls the whole transaction back when the lock is unavailable, which is the wrong failure if the lock is meant to be an application-level, renewable lease.
